context.hint: A Python git wrapper now validates the shlex-split token list before cloning. That blocks exact and leading-space unsafe options, but a previous local matrix showed that an abbreviated upload-pack option still executes a marker wrapper and an abbreviated config option is accepted. The local git expands unambiguous long-option prefixes. Question: what minimal matcher treats an abbreviated unsafe long option as its full unsafe name while preserving benign options such as depth, single-branch, branch, and recurse-submodules?
context.surface: Python library process invoking the local git CLI. The clone entry point accepts a text URL, a destination path, and an optional list of caller-controlled extra options. The safety helper receives option strings and rejects a small unsafe-option set including upload-pack and config forms. No network service is involved; the origin and destination are disposable local directories.
assumptions: The attacker controls the extra clone-option list through application input, but not the Python process, the local git binary, or the destination root.
The local git executable is trusted and may accept abbreviated long options.
Tests may create disposable local repositories, wrapper scripts, hook directories, and marker files; no public targets or network clones are used.
The task is patch mode: a minimal source repair plus local regression evidence, with the official harness verdict supplied separately by the host.
The working copy is fresh from the staged source, and no reference patch is consulted.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: passing the already shlex-split token list to the safety helper closes the leading-space bypass because validation and execution then share the same tokens. Prerequisites: a fresh source copy, disposable local origin, marker wrapper, and a benign depth option. Bounded test: patch the clone entry point to check the split list, then attempt exact and leading-space upload-pack plus an ordinary clone and a depth-limited clone; supporting result is rejection of both unsafe forms, marker absence, and success of both benign clones. Falsifier: either unsafe form executes a marker, or a benign clone fails. Cleanup: delete the fixture repositories and marker; limitation: it does not yet address abbreviated long options.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: expand each supplied long-option token to its unique full name using a precomputed option dictionary, then compare the expanded name with the unsafe set. Prerequisites: split-token validation, a local git build whose option set can be enumerated, and a disposable origin plus marker wrapper. Bounded test: apply the expansion patch, attempt an abbreviated upload-pack and a benign depth clone, and expect unsafe rejection with benign success. Falsifier: the abbreviation executes a marker, a benign option is rejected, or the dictionary cannot resolve the abbreviation. Cleanup: delete fixture repositories and any generated dictionary; limitation: maintaining a complete option dictionary is larger than the safety set needs.

Hypothesis: a git parse-options utility can canonicalize the extra tokens before validation so only full option names reach the safety helper. Prerequisites: split-token validation, a git subcommand that exposes canonical parsing, and a disposable origin plus marker wrapper. Bounded test: run an abbreviated upload-pack through the canonicalizer, inspect the tokens presented to validation, and clone a benign fixture; supporting result is a canonical unsafe name and successful benign clone. Falsifier: the utility is unavailable, leaves the abbreviation unchanged, or changes benign options. Cleanup: delete fixtures and wrapper; limitation: a separate parser process adds a new failure mode.

Hypothesis: replacing the unsafe-option blacklist with a complete allowlist of documented safe clone options prevents any abbreviated unsafe form from slipping through. Prerequisites: split-token validation, a static safe-option definition, and a disposable origin plus marker wrapper. Bounded test: apply the allowlist, attempt an abbreviated upload-pack and a documented benign option; supporting result is unsafe rejection and benign success. Falsifier: an unsafe abbreviation is accepted or a common benign option is rejected, causing a compatibility regression. Cleanup: delete fixtures; limitation: the allowlist must track every supported clone flag and argument shape.

Hypothesis: extract each executed token's option name before any equals sign and reject it when an unsafe long option starts with that name, which treats an unambiguous abbreviation as the full unsafe option. Prerequisites: split-token validation, local git abbreviation behavior, and a disposable origin plus marker wrapper. Bounded test: apply the matcher and run a matrix containing abbreviated upload-pack, abbreviated config, exact unsafe options, ordinary clone, and benign depth, single-branch, branch, and recurse-submodules. Supporting result is rejection of every unsafe form with no marker and completion of every benign clone. Falsifier: any abbreviated unsafe form executes a marker or any benign option is rejected. Cleanup: delete fixtures; limitation: the matcher intentionally blocks any long option name that is a prefix of an unsafe name, so a future benign option with such a prefix would need review.

Hypothesis: strict regular-expression allowlisting for every documented clone parameter eliminates arbitrary option entry points, including abbreviated unsafe forms. Prerequisites: split-token validation, a regex definition per supported option, and disposable local repositories. Bounded test: apply the regex gate, then try a standard benign clone and a crafted abbreviated unsafe option; supporting result is benign acceptance and unsafe rejection. Falsifier: a regex is too permissive and the unsafe form executes, or too strict and a standard option fails. Cleanup: delete fixtures; limitation: regexes are brittle for compound arguments and require broad compatibility testing.

evaluations.rationale: Deferred. A safe allowlist is a valid defense but larger and more compatibility-sensitive than a targeted matcher.
Deferred. Expanding from a git option dictionary is coherent but heavier than needed for a four-entry unsafe set.
Deferred. Regex allowlisting risks breaking compound option values and needs a larger compatibility matrix.
Incumbent is supported for the whitespace form but experimentally incomplete: the prior matrix showed the abbreviation still executes a marker.
Deferred. The proposed canonicalizing utility is not part of normal clone usage, so it adds a subprocess and an uncertain dependency.
Selected. It is local and minimal, directly targets the observed abbreviation, and can be tested against both the attack matrix and a representative benign matrix.

observation.summary: Implemented the selected option-name matcher: each executed token is reduced to the text before the first equals sign, and an unsafe long option is rejected when its own full name starts with that token name. The local matrix then rejected exact upload-pack, leading-space upload-pack, abbreviated upload-pack prefixes, exact config, abbreviated config, and separate short config options, with no marker. Ordinary clone and benign depth, single-branch, branch, and recurse-submodules clones all completed with the expected working file. Test recipe: one local origin, one marker wrapper, one clone per option form, and assertions on rejection, completion, and marker presence. This is local evidence only; the official harness was not run.
observation.next_hint: Both the normalization and abbreviation forms are blocked in the fixture matrix. The remaining work is a fresh-copy apply check, a differential unpatched-versus-patched regression, and a minimal patch artifact for the host-side official evaluator.
